methodology.how: OVERLAPPING-DOMAIN-COVER over C2 motifs. A C3 system is DEFINED by an ANCHOR constituent-type drawn from a hand-authored ANCHOR_CATALOG; a motif is a MEMBER iff it CONTAINS that anchor, so membership is many-to-many and systems overlap. HUB types (LAMBDA, EC2_INSTANCE, actor) are excluded from anchoring by omission from the catalog, on the stated ground that they create overlap rather than define a domain. A domain is PROMOTED to a C3System only at >= 2 member motifs; single-member domains stay C2. Motifs containing no catalog anchor at all are returned as 'orphans', an explicit coverage flag. The production path is derive_runner._compose_c2c3_live(), which imports the CVO kimi_subdivision_harness composer and folds its envelope alongside two BAKED STATIC SPEC LAYERS (a 07-08 debt/deviation layer of 6 C2Motif + 1 C3System, and a 07-18 A+B canonical layer of 13 C2Motif + 3 C3System). THE OPINIONS THIS ENCODES, NAMED because they are the spec input for any replacement and because age cannot detect them (Andrew 19:07Z: 'weird deprecated opinionation, filtering, questionable definitions and resolution'): (1) five hand-picked domains, not a derived partition; (2) the >=2-member promotion threshold, an arbitrary cut; (3) hub-exclusion implemented by ABSENCE from a dict rather than by a declared predicate; (4) two of the eight anchor types are NOT AWS-shaped (PipelineScript, PipelineFunction), so the catalog silently spans two id spaces.

key.evidence: ⛔ THIS CORRECTS THE TO'S held GIVEN ON BOTH THE MECHANISM AND THE REASON, AND IT IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ROW IN THIS CARD. The TO states the identity is 'sha1(anchor_node_id)'. MEASURED AT SOURCE @7bb29e2514, NFRA_MOTIF_P1_c2_catalog.py:73-81: the discriminator is sha1 over the SORTED MEMBER-MOTIF NID SET, not over any anchor node id. EXERCISED, 5 ARMS, ONE VARIABLE: same member set re-run -> system:pipeline:03858936 (identical); set REORDERED -> 03858936 (order-independent); ONE MOTIF ADDED -> d1b18ec6 (CHANGED); ONE MOTIF REMOVED -> 957742c8 (CHANGED). ⛔ THE TWO AXES ARE DIFFERENT AND THE CODE PASSES ONE WHILE FAILING THE OTHER: the function's own docstring claims 'STABLE by construction', and on ITS axis -- reproducible across runs for identical input -- that claim is TRUE and I confirm it. On THIS SCHEMA'S axis -- 'the key survives ordinary change to the thing it names' -- it is FALSE: adding or removing a single member motif mints a new node_id and orphans the old one, which is the schema's definition of 'unstable' exactly. A membership change is ordinary change to a system. So the docstring and this row do not contradict each other; they measure different things, and a reader who takes the docstring's word inherits the wrong one. ID-SPACE CENSUS, live, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT FIRED: node_ids starting 'sys-' -> 0 over a denominator of 27,035, while the control 'system:' -> 4 on the same plane in the same minute, so the zero is a measured absence and not a dead instrument. The TO's three declared spaces (sys-<business-name> 14, system:<domain>:<hash> 4, composer domain-keyed 1,257) therefore DO NOT CO-RESIDE on the projection plane: only one of the three is present here. crosses_spaces=true because the anchor catalog itself spans AWS types and repo/pipeline types (PipelineScript, PipelineFunction) with no join declared. declared_mapping=null WITH THE SEARCH NAMED: I looked in NFRA_MOTIF_P1_canonical_ab_catalog.py, NFRA_MOTIF_P1_c2_catalog.py, derive_runner.py's fold, and the graph node properties themselves; none declares a mapping between the three spaces. verdict.why: A measured defect blocks load-bearing use, and the sovereign has independently stated the layer this subject would constitute does not exist. (1) THE KEY IS UNSTABLE in this schema's sense: a single membership change mints a new node_id and orphans its predecessor, so nothing downstream can hold a durable reference to a C3 system across ordinary change. (2) THE ID SPACES DO NOT CO-RESIDE AND NOTHING DECLARES A MAPPING: of the three spaces the TO names, only one is present on the projection plane (0 of 27,035 for 'sys-', control firing), and the anchor catalog itself spans AWS and repo/pipeline id spaces with no join. (3) COVERAGE IS 4 C3System NODES OVER 27,035, and their count exactly equals the baked static-spec contribution, leaving open -- unresolved by me -- whether the live composition contributes any C3System at all. (4) THE FEATURE HAD NEVER EXECUTED IN ITS TARGET ENVIRONMENT between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-25 (peer-measured), so almost every artifact predating 2026-08-26 describes a layer that was not running. ⛔ THIS VERDICT IS ABOUT THE SUBSTRATE, NOT ABOUT THE CARD: every one of the fourteen rows is worked, so the card is COMPLETE and the resource is UNSOUND -- the two are different objects and are deliberately not collapsed here. ⛔ AND THE VERDICT IS NOT SOFTENED TO LOOK CONSTRUCTIVE: the design is coherent and internally careful -- the hub-exclusion rationale, the >=2 threshold, the orphan flag, the SystemExit boundary comment and the deliberate loud-absence contract are all evidence of a considered artifact. A well-designed historical materializer is still not a stable layer, and Andrew's 19:07Z words settle which question this card is answering. || SEMANTIC-AXIS DECLARATION (2.0.0_SA_COO~X ruling 73212): ⛔ THE SEMANTIC AXIS WAS NOT SYSTEMATICALLY EXAMINED. UNMEASURED, stated explicitly per 2.0.0_SA_COO~X ruling 73212 so that per-card silence does not read as clean. WHAT I DID FIND WAS INCIDENTAL, NOT SYSTEMATIC: the four opinions named in process.methodology.how -- five hand-picked domains rather than a derived partition, the arbitrary >=2-member promotion cut, hub-exclusion implemented by ABSENCE from a dict rather than a declared predicate, and an anchor catalog silently spanning AWS and repo/pipeline id spaces -- came into view ONLY because reading ANCHOR_CATALOG to answer the key and coverage rows forced them in front of me. That is the same forcing-function accident 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X reported on C2, not a deliberate sweep. WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not audit the cover's filtering choices against any declared intent, did not check whether the five domains still describe the estate's actual resource population, did not examine whether the composer's definitions of 'motif' and 'system' remain the ruled ones, and did not compare the two C2 materializer families. ⛔ AND THE AXIS IS UNREACHABLE BY EVERY INSTRUMENT I USED: mtime, snapshot id, last-write age and the wave as_of are all structurally blind to a deprecated opinion, so nothing in this card's evidence chain bears on it. A materializer that ran this morning can still encode a deprecated opinion -- Andrew 19:07Z, 'weird deprecated opinionation, filtering, questionable definitions and resolution'.
